title: Point-of-care lactate at emergency department triage for adults with suspected sepsis: an umbrella review of false reassurance, accuracy and false alarms
abstract: Objective: to synthesise published reviews of point-of-care lactate at emergency department triage for adults with suspected sepsis, with false reassurance as the primary outcome. Methods: umbrella review with a citation matrix, confidence ratings for each review and predictive values derived at local prevalence. Results and conclusions will be written after extraction.
introduction: Many reviews of lactate in sepsis disagree. They overlap heavily and most deserve low confidence, and none reports the two errors that matter at triage: false reassurance and false alarms.
methods: Searches by a librarian; two reviewers; extraction of outcomes, thresholds and sample types; critical appraisal of each review; corrected covered area; selection of one review per outcome and threshold; derivation of predictive values at local prevalence.
results: No data have been extracted yet. The report will present the review flow, the citation matrix, confidence ratings and tables of false reassurance, accuracy and false alarms by threshold.
discussion: The discussion will state what a normal and a raised lactate can justify at triage, how confident the evidence allows us to be, and what a local accuracy study would add.
limitations: Review-level evidence only; language restriction; dependence on an estimated local prevalence.
conclusion: To be written after extraction; it will be limited to what the reviews support.
summary: PRIOR-structured draft with results left empty.
